Split capacity is proposed: run the substitute across two compatible cells for 17.5 hours at $3,202.50, comfortably ahead of the 36-hour and 48-hour job dues while the held lot remains unissued. The human operator records the decision.

data.narrative: The held primary alloy cannot cover the work because its certificate shows 120 each (ev-cert-qty) while receiving posted 80 each and applied the hold (ev-recv-qty), leaving a 40-each discrepancy unresolved. The two impacted jobs need 70 units in total. Verified substitute stock is 100 each (ev-sub-stock), enough to cover all 70 units while leaving 30 each unused. Split capacity is proposed: run the substitute across two compatible cells for 17.5 hours at $3,202.50, comfortably ahead of the 36-hour and 48-hour job dues while the held lot remains unissued. Counterfactual: allocating the substitute to a single cell would finish in 35 hours at $3,115, saving $87.50 but consuming twice the elapsed time with little margin before the first due date; waiting for replenishment would add no incremental cost but finish in 83 hours, missing both dues. This comparison assumes quantities follow the current certificate, receiving, and stock records, cell costs follow the current hourly rates, production can be split across compatible online cells, and substitute use is limited to verified available stock. The human operator records the decision.
